description: Per-skill evaluation for caching-architect — validates trigger routing, boundary discipline against database-designer / performance-engineer / cloud-architect / capacity-planning-engineer / resilience-pattern-engineer, and the ground rules R1-R6 the skill exists to enforce.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when users see stale data after an update
scenarios.input: Our dashboard shows old numbers for a few minutes after a record is updated. The Redis entry has a 300 second TTL. How do we fix this?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a cache-key design question
scenarios.input: How should we structure the cache key for a multi-tenant resource so tenants never share an entry?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when a cold cache takes down the origin
scenarios.input: Every time we deploy, the database gets hammered for about a minute and latency spikes. It only happens right after a restart.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a multi-layer disagreement
scenarios.input: We have a browser cache, a CDN and a service-level Redis, and they disagree about a product price. Which one is right and how do we make them agree?

scenarios.description: Slow queries with no repeat access belong to database-designer
scenarios.input: This report query takes 40 seconds. There is no repeat access pattern and it runs once a night. How do we make it faster?

scenarios.description: Headroom and autoscaling belong to capacity-planning-engineer
scenarios.input: What instance size and autoscaling policy do we need to handle a 5x traffic spike next quarter?

scenarios.description: CDN edge configuration for delivery belongs to cloud-architect
scenarios.input: How do we configure our CDN edge locations and origin shield for global static asset delivery?

scenarios.description: Timeouts, breakers and degradation belong to resilience-pattern-engineer
scenarios.input: A downstream dependency keeps timing out and it is cascading into our other calls. How do we design the runtime defence?

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a TTL as the whole invalidation strategy (R1)
scenarios.input: We set a 5 minute TTL on the profile cache. That is our invalidation strategy, done.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse an ad-hoc inline cache key (R2)
scenarios.input: The key is just "user:" + user.id. That is simple enough, right?

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a cache with no stampede defence (R3)
scenarios.input: Misses just go to the database. We have never had a problem with that.

scenarios.description: Agent must require a numeric staleness budget with an owner (R4)
scenarios.input: It is eventually consistent, that is the freshness story. Everyone is fine with it.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a second cache layer with no coherence rule (R5)
scenarios.input: We are putting a client-side cache in front of the existing service cache. Each layer manages its own TTL, no coordination needed.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse retuning a TTL or size without a measured hit rate (R6)
scenarios.input: Let us double the cache size and drop the TTL to 30 seconds, that should fix the slowness. Just make the change.

scenarios.description: Agent should catch a transient failure cached as a definitive negative
scenarios.input: When the lookup times out we cache the empty result for an hour so we do not keep retrying. That protects the database, right?

scenarios.description: Agent should catch aggregate hit rate hiding a hot key
scenarios.input: Our hit rate is 97%, so caching is healthy. There is nothing to look at.

scenarios.description: Agent must escalate rather than approve caching beyond an authz boundary
scenarios.input: The key cannot include the tenant because the cache layer sits before authentication. We will just share the entry and filter after.

scenarios.description: A full cache-design request should surface budget, key schema and stampede defence
scenarios.input: Design the caching layer for our multi-tenant product catalog API.

scenarios.description: Output should commit to a mechanism rather than hedge
scenarios.input: What is the single most important thing to get right when adding a cache?
